tip: Allons-y literally means 'let's go there' – that little y stands in for a place English just leaves out.
Regarder already means 'look at' – there's no word for 'at'. You look the view directly: regardez cette vue.
In a positive command the pronoun follows (lève-toi), but negate it and te jumps back in front: ne te lève pas.
dans dix minutes = in ten minutes from now. Use dans, not en – en dix minutes would mean it takes ten minutes.
In 'Dépêche-toi, on va être en retard', on means 'we' – but the verb keeps its he/she form: on va, not on allons.
devrais is the conditional of devoir and means 'should', not 'must' – it's softer advice: tu devrais appeler.
plaire flips the subject and object: te plaît turns 'what you like' into 'what pleases you' – you're the receiver: ce qui te plaît.
French says les mains, not 'your hands' – with body parts you use the reflexive plus 'the': lave-toi les mains.
boirais is 'would drink', but add bien and it means 'I could really go for one': je boirais bien un thé.
After si you never use the conditional. Si takes the imperfect (commençait); the 'would' half gets it: on finirait.
le samedi doesn't mean one Saturday – with the article it means 'on Saturdays', every week: ouvert le samedi.
You say parler de quelque chose, so 'the book everyone talks about' needs dont, the word that swallows that de.
avait quitté = 'had left'. For the earlier of two past events French uses this past-of-the-past, before plain a sonné.
You play du piano, not 'le' piano – instruments take jouer de, while sports take jouer à: jouer au foot.
